method: sum of gzip -9 over each module in the route's rel="modulepreload" list, per file, never concatenated
tolerance_basis: 4 builds of identical source, route /, 2026-08-25, this repo: 49193 / 49198 / 49198 / 49205. Range 12 B, and the cause is named - SvelteKit stamps a version string into the entry chunk. 64 B is 5.3x that range; four samples underestimate a true range, so the multiple is the margin. Derived, not measured. If a build ever fails inside 64 B, re-derive it from more builds and more routes rather than nudging it.

/.why: Up 1,045 B because the operator console became three routes, and not one of those bytes is console code. Two things moved, both structural to SvelteKit: the shared entry chunk grew 394 B where the client manifest embeds the two new route nodes and the console layout node, and Svelte's own runtime was re-cut into more and smaller chunks, which costs gzip headers and cross-file matches. Every route preloads the entry, so every route pays. Measured 2026-08-30 on one Windows 11 dev machine, 12th Gen Intel Core i7-1265U, node v24.12.0, one session, the same worktree built twice back to back with only the changed source swapped: / 52,881 -> 53,926, /404 42,841 -> 43,811, /<date>/ 52,117 -> 53,149, /<date>/<topic>/ 52,211 -> 53,241, /archive/ 53,517 -> 54,545, /evals/ 43,794 -> 44,766. The control needs no interpretation: the origin/main arm PASSED the gate outright, every route inside the 64 B tolerance of its committed record, so this machine reproduces the record and the delta is the change rather than the toolchain. The four new modules on each reading route were opened and read - they are Svelte internals and none of them mentions the console. What the bytes buy a reader is nothing, and that is the honest statement: they are the price of an operator surface that was 8,794px tall becoming three pages that can each be weighed on their own. Confirm against the CI site job before trusting the absolute figures: a local Windows build has read 81 to 87 B under CI on every route before now.

/<date>/.why: Up 1,032 B for the console route split. See the record on / for the paired measurement and the cause: a 394 B growth in the shared entry chunk, where the client manifest embeds the two new console route nodes, plus Svelte runtime chunks re-cut into more and smaller files. No console module reaches this page. In proportion, a day page is 350,638 gzipped bytes of HTML against 53,149 of first-load JavaScript, so this is 0.3 percent of what the route actually transfers.

/<date>/<topic>/.why: Up 1,030 B for the console route split. Same cause and same paired measurement as / and /<date>/: the shared entry chunk grows where the client manifest embeds the new route nodes, and Svelte's runtime chunks are re-cut. No console module reaches this page.

/404.why: Runtime and app shell and nothing route-specific. This is the floor every other route sits on, which is what makes it the cleanest reading of the console route split: up 970 B and 15 -> 19 modules, on a page that renders no item, no ledger and no chart. The four added modules were opened and read - Svelte internals, none of them naming the console - and the entry chunk itself went 2,709 -> 3,103 B, which is the client manifest embedding two new route nodes and a layout node. The rest is gzip overhead from two shared chunks becoming five. Measured 2026-08-30 on one Windows 11 dev machine, 12th Gen Intel Core i7-1265U, node v24.12.0, one session, origin/main and this branch built back to back on the same worktree; the origin/main arm passed the gate on every route, so the machine agrees with the record. This is the same mechanism this record has carried since 2026-08-29 for the chart engine: a route added to the app grows the manifest the entry embeds, and every route preloads the entry.

/archive/.why: Up 1,028 B for the console route split. Same cause and same paired measurement as / and /404: the shared entry chunk grows where the client manifest embeds the new console route nodes, and Svelte's runtime chunks are re-cut into more and smaller files. No console module reaches this page.

/console/.why: Pipelines - the first of the console's three routes, and the only one that loads the chart engine. It answers one question and refuses the others: did the runs work, which feeds broke, and what each stage cost. It draws the standing band and the navigation strip, one window control the whole page obeys, a run-health strip and donut, a feed list ranked by distance to a rest, a Sankey of the stage funnel, per-day stage timings, the failure mix by stage, the item-telemetry viewport with its band split and failure ledger, a source-length range plot, a published skyline, the per-article cost plot and the chart arm's two thresholds. DOWN 1,401 B against the 90,469 the single console page recorded, because the throughput trend, the eleven measure cards, their sparklines and the daily model table all left for /console/model/ - and that is more than the 394 B the shared entry chunk gained from the split. Measured 2026-08-30 on one Windows 11 dev machine, 12th Gen Intel Core i7-1265U, node v24.12.0, one session, origin/main built first and this branch second on the same worktree: the control read 90,473 B at 19 modules, 4 B over its committed record and inside the 64 B tolerance, so the machine reproduces the record and this delta is the change.

/console/machine/.why: Machine - the hardware the model ran on. It ships almost empty on purpose: the pipeline has written state/runtime-counters.csv since 2026-08-26 and no page has ever read a cell of it, so the route exists before its panels do and says what is missing once at the top and once per named panel. A route that hid itself until it had data would be a route nobody knew to check. The bytes are the app shell, the band and the strip, and no chart engine: 52,110 B at 25 modules against the 43,811 the empty /404 pays, so the whole cost of this route over the shell is 8,299 B. It draws no window control, because nothing on it is windowed yet. Measured 2026-08-30 on one Windows 11 dev machine, 12th Gen Intel Core i7-1265U, node v24.12.0, in the same session and the same build as the other two console routes.

/console/model/.why: Model - what the model wrote, how long it took, and what it got wrong. It carries the protected h2 `What the model did` verbatim, the throughput trend with its per-day spread candles, the eleven measure cards with a sparkline each, and the daily table behind a disclosure. It loads the chart engine for the throughput trend, which is why it is 18,185 B over /console/machine/ and 26,484 B over the empty /404. It draws a window control, because the card lines follow the window, but it prices no month files: every day it draws is already inlined, so no preset costs a fetch. Measured 2026-08-30 on one Windows 11 dev machine, 12th Gen Intel Core i7-1265U, node v24.12.0, in the same session and the same build as the other two console routes.

/evals/.why: Runtime and shell plus the stub that moves an old bookmark to /console/. Up 972 B for the console route split, on a page that draws nothing at all - which is the second clean reading of the cause, beside /404. See the record on / for the paired measurement: the shared entry chunk grows where the client manifest embeds the two new console route nodes and the layout node, and Svelte's runtime chunks are re-cut into more and smaller files. No console module reaches this page.
